scope: Actual GMGN buy/sell synchronous signing and RPC are moved off-loop with explicit caller, journal and runtime shutdown ownership. All irreversible provider/signing/RPC side effects are replaced by synthetic doubles; operator signing and network requests are not invoked.
user_objective: Keep exact 0.1 SOL paper entries, scanner/monitor responsiveness and the existing uncapped extreme-runner objective. This closes one execution-lifecycle risk, not profitable signals, production execution or captured financial gains.
findings: Both async GMGN operations called sign_and_send synchronously; RPC waits could block the shared event loop, including independent position monitoring and discovery/control tasks.

A bare to_thread worker task can survive cancellation of its caller. If the caller releases its intent/position scope or publishes stopped before the thread settles, existing recovery logic can observe an execution still in flight.

The executor's asyncio bridge can clone TimeoutError and discard original reconciliation attributes. Initial synthetic regression detected this; an explicit outcome envelope preserves the original result/error object.
The actual seller GMGN fallback used token_addr instead of its canonical token_mint, unlike the Jupiter path. The request could target another address alias.

implementation.off_loop: Run the callable exactly once on the existing executor, carrying a copied context. Use a private executor Future, not a worker Task exposed to asyncio.run bulk task cancellation. No provider re-route, new signed order or retry is added.
implementation.ownership: Register every worker per event loop. Shield its Future, retain the original caller until settlement, retrieve failures and propagate the original cancellation/interruption afterward, even after repeated cancellation. Existing buy entry scope and actual sell guard remain active while the worker runs; uncertain completed/live results remain in their durable prepared journals and cannot be replayed as no-fill.
implementation.queued_cancellation: Reject dispatch from a cancelling owner. A short locked start gate skips a cancelled worker that has not started its callable. Already-started work is joined rather than represented as absent. Cancellation during read-only route acquisition creates no execution worker.
implementation.result_identity: Transport the original callable result or BaseException in a private outcome envelope; preserve arguments, keyword arguments, context and custom error identity. On a cancelled owner, the original cancellation wins after the worker settles; no result is invented or promoted to a confirmed fill.
implementation.shutdown: Open a checked execution generation at actual runtime startup. After supervised owners/background/social/research cleanup, close dispatch and join all registered workers before publishing stopped. A generation cannot reopen while previous owners remain. Shutdown cancellation cannot abandon the remaining workers.
implementation.canonical_sell: The actual GMGN seller fallback consumes token_mint, matching its quote/validation path, and retains exact integer token quantity. Existing live-price/quantity/finality acceptance remains separate.
implementation.unchanged: No personal configuration, trading gate, order size, live activation, model training/promotion, policy activation or runner take-profit ceiling is changed. The operator signer is replaced directly in test namespace dictionaries without invoking the package's lazy signer import.
